answer: Divergent-challenge identity lottery: each identity must publish a unique, signed sable seed before acting, and the network assigns it a challenge drawn from a shared relic of prior entropy. Clones cannot diverge—copying a seed forces the duplicate onto the same trellis of challenges, so the second claimant collides and both are frozen. An attacker must therefore generate and defend independent divergence histories for every identity, paying full compute and detection risk per clone rather than one registration cost.
